I'm interested in the mathematics behind machine learning, in optimization,
and in efficiency: how small a model can be and still work, and how fast it
can be served. I'm also interested in Arabic-language AI.

I'm an AI instructor at SDAIA Academy, where I write and teach AI courses:
800+ contact hours, 1,200+ trainees, from developers to non-technical staff.

## Courses

- **Building Gen AI Apps**: LLM applications end to end: RAG, tool calling,
  agents, model adaptation, guardrails and deployment.
- **Computer Vision for Developers**: detection with YOLO, ONNX/TensorRT
  export, INT8 quantization, real-time pipelines.
- **Time Series Analysis & Forecasting**: a three-day practical course built
  on *Forecasting: Principles and Practice*.
- **Modern Data Engineering** (delivered): DuckDB, dlt, Polars, dbt, Dagster,
  Iceberg, Spark.
- **AI at Work**: Arabic workshops on turning repeated work into reusable AI
  workflows.
- **Intro to Robotics**: robotics for school students, with interactive
  browser simulations.
- **Robot Rockstars**: a five-week robotics bootcamp for WRO RoboMission,
  LEGO SPIKE Prime programmed in Python.

## Projects

[Arabic Language Modeling](https://github.com/NaifMersal/Arabic-Language-Modeling)
: N-gram, LSTM, Transformer and Mamba, parameter-matched at ~15M on 6.1 GB of
  Arabic Wikipedia. Perplexities landed at 93–95: at this scale the
  architecture barely matters.

[Arabic Legal Assistant](https://github.com/NaifMersal/Legal-assistant)
: Arabic legal RAG with a hybrid retriever; relational recall@20 from 44% to 58%.

[MFER](https://github.com/NaifMersal/MFER)
: Multimodal emotion recognition: Emotion2Vec audio features fused with a
  Vision Transformer, competitive with the state of the art on RAVDESS.

[swift911](https://github.com/NaifMersal/swift911)
: Voice-based emergency reporting: speech recognition, NLP and an agent that
  extracts incident details for dispatch.

**Small CNNs**
: An exploratory search over 100+ compact CNN designs. Models of 0.4M–0.7M
  parameters reach 60% ImageNet top-1, trained in float16 on a 4 GB GPU.

**LLM serving homelab**
: 3× RTX 3090. I benchmark llama.cpp, vLLM and ExLlamaV3 across speculative
  decoding (MTP, n-gram), tensor vs. layer parallelism, and layer offloading.

**CourseOS**
: A LangGraph multi-agent system for course authoring. Agent drafts reach
  roughly 60–65% of final quality, then I revise them.
